pr_title: SHAKE documentation updates for default output length.
pr_body:
Fixes #18586

In order to not break existing applications the OpenSSL documentation
related to SHAKE has been updated.
~~The openssl dgst commandline app will log a warning to stderr if
SHAKE128 is used without the -xoflen option.~~

Background:

All digests algorithms (including XOF's) use the bitlen as the default output length.
This results in a security strength of bitlen / 2.

This means that SHAKE128 will by default have an output length of 16
bytes and a security strength of 64 bits.

For SHAKE256 the default output length is 32 bytes and has a security
strength of 128 bits.

This behaviour was present in 1.1.1 and has been duplicated in the
provider SHAKE algorithms for 3.0.

The SHAKE XOF algorithms have a security strength of
min(bitlen, output xof length in bits / 2).

issue_context.title: SHAKE is Made Half its Security Level by Default in OpenSSL DGST
issue_context.body:
128 or 256 in SHAKE128 or SHAKE256 is not the length, it's the security level, i.e. SHA256 or SHA512 are 128 and 256 accordingly. SHAKE, when not double the size its said security level, gives half the promised security. [Quote](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/crypto/sha3), "SHAKE256, with an output length of at least 64 bytes, provides 256-bit security against all attacks." Therefore the default of OpenSSL DGST is not properly set and makes a hash function twice as weak. This is essentially a bug, a defect, in the default length setting, that came from misreading of the actual specification.

Many people may trust OpenSSL and might use the default, please fix.
comments: The dgst util should probably not support shake in the first place.

**OTC: is this a bug?  What's the fix?**

The problem is deeper.  The shake digests return these lengths as their output size.  We could:
1. accept things as they are (i.e. not a bug)
2. change the output sizes (double or zero)
3. update the dgst command to require an `xoflen` argument when given an XOF digest
4. something else?
**OTC: Because there might be already users depending on the existing default length we cannot change it. We just need to document that the defaults doesn't give the expected security level.**

> OTC: Because there might be already users depending on the existing default length we cannot change it.

That's a really suboptimal decision IMO. Users might just as well be depending on the fact that it does what it says on the tin, and likely in larger (though silent) numbers than those who depend on an unintentional degradation of the security level.

The decision was made because the EVP_DigestFinal API does not allow for passing output buffer length. That means the change could potentially trigger a security issue by overflowing the existing buffer. So no, we cannot change the decision.

review_comments: So is this something that can be supported in some future version?
